item.content:encoded:
Feels a lot, and I mean a LOT like SCP-885-J. Though there are funny moments, at times you're just fission for yaks, especially with an inconsistent and heavy handed "hilarious" reaction.
Then you've got the object class. I personally love it; it sets the tone with the nonstandard object class by telling is its intrinsic nature is "Loud and messy." The loud part, however, is not meaningfully expounded upon by Yerry's nature, as any mention of his volume is... "loud." Compare to your messy class, which is backed up by him leaving dead bodies everywhere, spreading his metabolic waste products, etc.
Of particular note is footnotes 9 and 10. There you've got a beautiful example of showing something which furthers the roommate's frustration and then go ahead and tell us how to feel as well.
To be honest, most of the footnotes don't contribute much of meaning. Footnote 1 you might have something good with "dropping dem [sic] gram negs everywhere," But how is he loud? In what way?
Footnote 2's very good. This is the only true evidence that Yerry's loud, and it also tells us the general nature of his loudness. I like it.
Footnote 3's general idea is good, but execution leaves me feeling "meh." The class-c amnestics bit covers everything you need, but might need different phrasing. 'Dr. Mike's request for bi-weekly class-c amnestic administrations is currently pending.' or some such thing. This shows the promiscuity of the bacteria and reinforces just how bad it is.
Footnote 4 is. Bad. It's a stupid name by it's nature, and if you just put it in quotation marks the whole object we'd get that idea.
Footnote 5 is a bit contrary to the idea it's footnoting. The anecdote, sans 'He eats EVERYTHING,' is humorous enough, but suggests a bit more ravenous-than-usual appetite which should appear on the documentation, mostly for the sake of leaving its truth up in the air while still being descriptively accurate.
Footnote 6 is topical, includes a catchphrase-esque introduction, and just communicates frustration over lost money in a bland way. The sentence it footnotes communicates this very, very well; a followup sentence in the actual SCP, possibly involving a request for remuneration by Dr. Mike to Yerry for christmas, also communicates what Mike lost beyond losing that money.
Footnote 7 sucks. The fact they're puns communicates their base-level humor, and we get that Yerry shouldn't be able to talk. It's the job of the Foundation, even in -J's, to explain what's happening. It's nonsensical by nature. We don't need Mike's thoughts on how nonsensical it is.
Footnote 8 is just. Useless. We get it. Mike's upset. Where the fuck do the rats go? Putting a number on exactly how many rats might also make us more sympathetic to Mike.
So onto the actual text. It's mostly pretty good; I only take real issue with two sentences. First is "The entity occasionally invites that fucking weird dude with the mask to "hang out" and smoke dat dank shit, leaving that godawful smell on everything." Why isn't "dat dank shit" in quotation marks? 049 makes sense, and absolutely helps the humor, but why "fucking weird"? The second is "SCP-1347-1353-J is currently involved in a romantic relationship with ████ ██████, who is very loud during promiscuous activities." Again, don't tell us that she's loud. You've almost or actually communicated this with "A total disregard for Yerry's roommates while they are sleeping." in a much better way.

Tl;Dr It's mediocre, and while there are scraps which show what it could become, it ultimately lacks in execution. -1 for now, but it's close to being good.
